name: Long running tasks
description:
**Conversation summary (5 lines)**

1. You asked for an initial **long-running tasks** design: a complex objective split into sub-tasks, managed by a board + budget + profile, run to completion (all done / budget out / stopped), and resumable after a restart.
2. I reviewed the API and wrote `docs/long-running-tasks.md` (v2), then re-anchored it on your notes: a **main task** carrying the objective, budget, profile and stop switch, with every descendant sharing that root.
3. You approved the prep work as **LRT-0** and reported it done; I audited it and found it only **partly** landed (storage v2, `root_id`, cost roll-up, `find_by_id` ✅ — `AGENT_DONE_WORD`, dead `generate_tasks`, duplicate startup/routes ❌), so cleanup became **WP0**.
4. Cards created for the milestone went to the **wrong project** (root `codx-junior`, `d4e4b4a9`) and were invisible to `codx-api`, so WP0–WP4 had to be recreated inside `codx-api` storage.
5. You then told me to **start the tasks in order inside sprint `codx-junior-agents`**; WP0–WP4 now exist on that sprint (WP0 `1d081b9d` → WP4 `4582ae9c`) with the execution captured in `docs/long-running-tasks-plan.md`.

⚠️ Note: that last step stopped mid-verification — I had not yet confirmed each card's sprint membership and status, nor started WP0 processing. That is the pending action.

messages.content:
We need an initial version of long running tasks. Given a complex tasks it will split into small tasks and process. It can generate more tasks as needed.
Goal is to return a (depending on the task) a functional work that user can test and review.

Examples: 
 - "Create a website with a and b that does c"
 - "Review all UI compoenents and generate a catching mobile UI"

We'll create a board for the long running task and assign a budget and a profile to manage the process, all sub tasks generated will be in the same board and the profile will decide when the task is done. Tasks will be processed until:
 -  All tasks are done
 - Board runs out of budget
 - Stopped by user

Long running tasks must be resumed in case of an app reset/power-off. Processing will continue until the conditions are met.

Review all codx-junior API and suggest the best way to implement it.

I'll start by mapping the project and locating the pieces involved in task processing, boards, budgets, and background execution.## 1. Review & Understand the Task **Objective (my reading):** - Introduce **long‑running tasks (LRT)**: one *complex objective* is split into small tasks that are processed one after another, and the run may **generate new tasks** while it goes. - The unit of organisation is a **kanban board**: the board holds the budget and the **profile that manages the process**; all generated sub‑tasks live on that board. - The managing profile is the one that **decides the run is finished**. - Processing continues until: **all tasks done**, **board budget exhausted**, or **stopped by the user**. - The run must **survive an app reset / power‑off** and continue automatically. - Deliverable of this step: **review the existing API and propose the implementation** (not a full code dump). **Acceptance criteria I will hold the design against:** 1. Start a run from a free‑text objective → board + budget + profile are recorded and the run starts by itself. 2. Sub‑tasks are created/updated by the managing profile through existing tooling, all on the run's board. 3. Execution is **out of the request path** (the API has a 30s middleware timeout) and survives restart with no manual "resume" click. 4. Exactly **one** worker advances a given run, even with several API/background processes. 5. Budget is enforced **hard** (never exceeded, not just reported) and accounted even if messages are deleted. 6. Stop/pause is honoured promptly, mid‑turn, and the stopped state is durable. 7. Every tick is observable (chat events + socket + control chat transcript) and cost is attributable per run. --- ## 2. Information Gathering — API review (facts found, with paths) The relevant machinery already exists; LRT should be **composition, not a new subsystem**. Key findings: | Area | Reality in this repo | Consequence for LRT | |---|---|---| | Task = chat | `codx/junior/db.py::Chat` (`board`, `column`, `sprints`, `status`, `mode`, `profiles`, `cost`, `estimation_cost`), persisted as `.codx/tasks///..json` (`chat_manager.py::get_chat_file`) | Sub‑tasks are plain chats; no new entity needed | | Creation core | `codx/junior/task_manager.py::TaskManager.create_task` — mandatory `name`+`description`, nothing inherited | The supervisor must create fully‑specified tasks; no AI auto‑split exists anymore (`ChatEngineActions.generate_tasks` was removed) | | Catalogue | `.codx/tasks/kanban.json` `{version, boards:{name:{id,title,description,columns[{id,title,color}],active,last_update,parent_id,type}}, tags}`; read/write via `ChatManager.load_kanban/save_kanban`; board/column/sprint CRUD + `validate_task_destination` in `codx/junior/tools/project_manager_tools.py` | Board entry is the natural place for **run configuration**; board *name* is also the folder (`get_chat_file`) | | Budget primitive | `Chat.estimation_cost` + monotonic `Chat.cost`; enforcement in `codx/junior/ai/smol/smol_agent.py` (`_cost_limit_exceeded`, `_accumulated_chat_cost`, stops **before** executing more tools, emits `ESTIMATION_COST_EXCEEDED_MSG`); accumulation in `ChatManager.add_message/update_message/_accumulate_message_cost` | Per‑task hard cap already works; the **board** cap must be aggregated and pushed down as `estimation_cost` per task | | Execution entry | `CODXJuniorSession.chat_with_project(chat=...)` → `ChatEngineActions` → `ChatEngine.chat_with_project` (cancellation token registered per `chat.doc_id`, `ChatEventBridge` persists increments) | One "unit of work" = one `chat_with_project` on one task | | Cancellation | `codx/junior/ai/cancellation.py::CANCELLATION_REGISTRY` (by `chat_id` or `token_id`), exposed at `POST /api/chat/cancel` (`codx/junior/api/chat.py`) | "Stop by user" = durable flag **+** cancel the in‑flight token | | Background execution | `codx/junior/background.py`: `start_background_services(stop_event)` starts **daemon threads** only when `CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND` is set; loops use `check_projects` + `ThreadPoolExecutor`; async work is run per thread with `asyncio.run(...)` (`run_project_check_thread`) | The LRT loop belongs here, with a per‑run lock; **the plain API process does not run background loops** | | HTTP constraints | `app.py`: `GLOBAL_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30` middleware → 504; routers are **auto‑discovered** (`codx/junior/api/__init__.py::discover_routers`, every module exporting `router` is mounted at `/api`) | LRT endpoints must be **start/stop/status only**; long work never inside the request; new router file is auto‑registered | | Planning/status vocabulary | `codx/junior/planning_manager.py`: `STATUS_ORDER = [todo, doing, onhold, done, rejected]`, `DONE_STATUSES = {done}`, `CLOSED_STATUSES = {done, rejected}`; `ChatStatusEvent` appended on every real transition (`ChatManager._register_status_change`) | "All tasks done" must use **these** constants, never a second list | | UI hooks | `PlanningManager.query_tasks/build_dashboard` (`POST /api/planning/tasks/query`, `/dashboard`), `/api/kanban` GET/POST, `ChatEventBridge` + `message_event` | Board progress and per‑task status are already renderable; only run state needs a new view | **Blocking defects found while reviewing (must be handled before/with LRT):** 1. `codx/junior/kanban/__init__.py` imports `codx.junior.kanban.board_status_review`, **which does not exist in the repo** → `import codx.junior.kanban` raises. LRT must not import that package (and the import should be repaired separately). 2. `codx/junior/app.py` still contains legacy handlers that call removed code (e.g. `/api/chats/sub-tasks` → `codx_junior_session.generate_tasks`) and duplicated `@app.on_event("startup")`. `codx/junior/api/chat.py` also defines `PUT /chats/mark-seen/...` twice. Not caused by LRT, but the LRT router must not add to the drift. 3. `kanban.json` writes are **read‑modify‑write with no lock** (`ChatManager.save_kanban`), while the UI writes the same file. Run *runtime* state must therefore **not** live in `kanban.json`. 4. Board *name* is the storage folder (`get_chat_file`), and `project_manager_tools` still `shutil.move`s folders on rename. Runs should therefore key on the **board `id`** and never trigger renames. --- ## 3. Change Proposal & Refinement ### 3.1 Core idea A **run** is a *board + configuration + durable state machine*, advanced by a **single "tick" at a time**: ```mermaid flowchart TD T[Tick] --> L{lock ok?} L -->|no| X[skip] L -->|yes| S{state RUNNING?} S -->|no| X S -->|yes| B{spent >= budget?} B -->|yes| BE[STOP: budget_exhausted] B -->|no| A{actionable task?} A -->|yes| R[recover/claim task -> estimation_cost = remaining
chat_with_project(task)] R --> U[persist attempt + heartbeat] U --> T2[next tick] A -->|no| SUP[supervisor turn on control chat
create/move/verify tasks, or finish] SUP --> D{finished?} D -->|yes| CP[STOP: completed + delivery report] D -->|no| T2 ``` Why this shape: - **Crash‑safe by construction**: state is on disk, and the only in‑flight unit is one chat turn, which is itself persisted incrementally (`ChatEventBridge.maybe_persist_stream`). A restart resumes the same tick. - **Idempotent**: a tick re‑reads chats from disk; nothing is held in memory between ticks. - **Budget‑honest**: costs are read from `Chat.cost` (monotonic, survives message deletion) and the remaining budget is pushed down into `Chat.estimation_cost` so `SmolAgent` stops the individual turn before overspending. - **No new scheduler**: reuse the existing daemon‑thread + `asyncio.run` pattern; no Celery/APScheduler. ### 3.2 Data model (two stores, on purpose) 1. **Run configuration — board entry in `tasks/kanban.json`** (UI‑editable, already the catalogue): ```json { "id": "uuid", "title": "Website a+c", "type": "long_running", "long_run": { "enabled": true, "objective": "Create a website with a and b that does c", "profile": "tech_lead", "budget_cxjcoins": 25.0, "per_task_budget_cxjcoins": 2.0, "supervisor_reserve_cxjcoins": 2.5, "max_tasks": 40, "max_iterations": 200, "task_mode": "agent", "column": "tasks", "verify_column": "review", "created_at": "...", "created_by": "user@x" } } ``` 2. **Run runtime state — separate file** `.codx/long_running/.json` (atomic `os.replace`, own lock), so UI edits of `kanban.json` never race: ```python LongRunState: board_id, board, status (running|paused|stopped|completed|budget_exhausted|failed|stalled) attempts: {task_id: int} current_task_id, step_started_at, last_tick_at, ticks spent_cxjcoins (checkpoint; recomputed from chats each tick) stop_reason, summary, delivery_report_message_id lock: {pid, host, heartbeat_at} ``` ### 3.3 Loop and stop conditions - **Actionable task** = `status in (todo, doing)` on the board with `attempts < MAX_ATTEMPTS (3)`, ordered `priority, due_date, sort_index`. Exactly **one at a time** per run (predictable budget, no worktree/board contention). `max_parallel` can be added later behind the same tick. - **Recovery**: if `current_task_id` is set, the process died, and no `CANCELLATION_REGISTRY` token exists → `attempts += 1`, re‑run. After `MAX_ATTEMPTS` → `status="onhold"` + supervisor comment (`project_manager(action='request_help')`). - **Budget**: `spent = Σ chat.cost` over chats on the board **including the control chat**; before each turn ensure `spent < budget`, else `budget_exhausted`. Because the supervisor also costs money, `supervisor_reserve_cxjcoins` is kept aside so the run can always produce the final report. - **Completion**: only the **managing profile** may finish, via an explicit tool call (`long_running(action="finish", summary=...)`). Safety nets: `stalled` after `STAGNATION_TICKS` (e.g. 3) supervisor turns that neither create nor move a task, `failed` on unrecoverable errors, `max_tasks/max_iterations` guards against infinite self‑expansion. - **User stop/pause**: written to state (durable) **and** `CANCELLATION_REGISTRY.cancel(current_task_id)` to abort mid‑turn. `resume` clears the flag; nothing else is recreated. ### 3.4 Execution placement & single‑worker guarantee - New loop `check_long_running_runs()` in `background.py`, own thread, interval ~5s, started next to `check_projects` (same `RUN_BACKGROUND_PROCESSES` flag, same "runs in the background process" contract). Each run advances inside its own thread with `asyncio.run(runner.tick())`, mirroring `run_project_check_thread`. - **Single worker**: lock file `.codx/long_running/.lock` created with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` containing `{pid, host}`; a stale lock (heartbeat older than `LOCK_TIMEOUT`, e.g. 10 min) is taken over. This is what makes restart recovery and multi‑process safe. ### 3.5 API surface (follows the project REST conventions) Identity in the URL (`board_id`), `project_id` as **query** param, bodies describe the resource only: | Method | Path | Body / effect | |---|---|---| | `GET` | `/api/long-running` | list runs (config + state + progress/budget) | | `POST` | `/api/long-running` | `{objective, budget_cxjcoins, profile, board?, column?, task_mode?, max_tasks?, max_iterations?, per_task_budget_cxjcoins?, supervisor_reserve_cxjcoins?, auto_start?}` → creates board (via catalogue helpers) + control chat + state | | `GET` | `/api/long-running/{board_id}` | detail (state, spent/remaining, task counts, current task) | | `POST` | `/api/long-running/{board_id}/pause` \| `/resume` \| `/stop` | durable flag (+ cancel in‑flight token on stop) | | `POST` | `/api/long-running/{board_id}/tick` | one manual tick (debug/testing) | | socket | `codx-junior-long-running` | step events: `tick`, `task_started`, `task_done`, `finished`, `budget_exhausted` | ### 3.6 Tool surface One new unified tool `long_running` (same pattern as `project_manager`), registered in `codx/junior/tools/__init__.py` with `settings` + `session` injection: - `start` — a normal chat can turn an objective into a run ("Create a website with a and b…"). - `status` — progress/budget for the managing profile. - `finish` — **only** the run's own profile on the run's own control chat may declare completion (validated server‑side). - `add_task` — kept as a thin alias over `project_manager(action='create_task')` so the supervisor has one obvious verb. The supervisor's system prompt (new `codx/junior/profiles/long_running.profile`) states: objective, budget remaining, task table, and the rules — *split only what is needed now*, *always leave a verifiable next step*, *always end with a "how to test" task*, *call `finish` only when the objective is demonstrably achieved*. ### 3.7 Alternatives considered and rejected | Alternative | Why not | |---|---| | Keep the whole loop in memory / in the request | 30s middleware timeout; dies on restart | | Encode the run only in `kanban.json` | UI read‑modify‑write race; runtime fields are noise for the board editor | | New `LongRun` entity in `db.py` (TinyDB) | Chats already carry cost/status/board; a second entity duplicates persistence and breaks `/api/planning` | | Re‑introduce AI sub‑task generation (`generate_tasks`) | Explicitly removed by design (tasks are created with all their information) | | Drive from `Chat.mode="agent"` recursion (`AGENT_DONE_WORD`) | Single chat, no board budget, no new tasks, not resumable per task | | Celery/APScheduler worker | New infra and deployment; existing daemon‑thread pattern is enough for v1 | ### 3.8 Risks / edge cases - **Self‑expansion** → `max_tasks`, `max_iterations`, stagnation detection, budget floor. - **Board renamed by user** → state keyed by `board_id`, folder moves only through the catalogue (a rename mid‑run must pause the run). - **Two `kanban.json` writers** → only the config key is written on start/stop, and always through `ChatManager.save_kanban` with a lock/short retry. - **Money accounting drift** → always recompute `spent` from chats; the checkpoint is informational only. - **`estimation_cost` shrink** → set once per turn from `remaining` (never above it), so a resumed task cannot exceed the board budget. - **Background process disabled** (`CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND` unset) → runs sit in `running` until a worker exists: the status endpoint must surface "waiting for worker". --- ## 4. Changes Summary **New files** | File | Contents | |---|---| | `codx/junior/long_running/__init__.py` | public exports (`LongRunningService`, `LongRunningRunner`, models) | | `codx/junior/long_running/models.py` | `LongRunStatus`, `LongRunConfig`, `LongRunState`, `LongRunProgress`, request/response models (pydantic, `ConfigDict`, docs) | | `codx/junior/long_running/store.py` | state file + lock (atomic `os.replace`, `O_CREAT\|O_EXCL`, stale takeover), board config read/write helpers over `ChatManager.load_kanban/save_kanban` | | `codx/junior/long_running/service.py` | `start / pause / resume / stop / status / list`; board + control chat creation via `project_manager_tools` helpers; config↔state↔chats aggregation (`spent`, counts, current task) | | `codx/junior/long_running/runner.py` | `tick()`: recovery, task selection, `estimation_cost` push‑down, `session.chat_with_project`, supervisor turn, stop conditions, events | | `codx/junior/api/long_running.py` | the router (auto‑discovered by `discover_routers`) | | `codx/junior/tools/long_running_tools.py` | `long_running` tool (`start/status/finish/add_task`) + `LONG_RUNNING_TOOL_JSON` | | `codx/junior/profiles/long_running.profile` | supervisor instructions (objective → tasks → verify → finish) | **Modified files** | File | Change | |---|---| | `codx/junior/background.py` | add `check_long_running_runs()` + `run_long_running_tick()` and start the thread in `start_background_services` (guarded by the same flag/stop event) | | `codx/junior/tools/__init__.py` | register `long_running` in `TOOLS` (`async: True`, `project_settings: True`, `session: True`) | **No changes** to `db.py`, `chat_manager.py`, `smol_agent.py`, `planning_manager.py`: `Chat.cost`/`estimation_cost`/`status_history`/`tags` (`long_run:`) already carry everything. **Out of scope (separate fix, still flagged):** the broken `codx/junior/kanban/__init__.py` import, and the duplicated/legacy handlers in `app.py` and `api/chat.py`. --- ## 5. The Changes Not written yet, deliberately: four decisions change the shape of `runner.py` and `service.py`, and getting them wrong would mean rewriting the loop. 1. **Budget unit** — cxjcoins via `Chat.estimation_cost`/`Chat.cost` (my recommendation), or a task counter ("N task turns")? 2. **Concurrency per run** — strictly one task turn at a time (my recommendation), or `max_parallel` from day one? 3. **Where the worker lives** — extend `background.py` (only active when `CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND` is set, i.e. the supervisor/background process), or an always‑on thread in the API process? 4. **Config location** — board entry `long_run` key in `kanban.json` + runtime state in `.codx/long_running/.json` (my recommendation), or a single separate file for everything? Confirm (or correct) these four and I will produce the initial version as complete file contents in the order `models.py` → `store.py` → `service.py` → `runner.py` → `api/long_running.py` → `tools/long_running_tools.py` → `background.py`/`tools/__init__.py` patches.

    """
    Cancel an in-flight chat request by chat_id or cancellation token UUID.

    Expected payload (at least one key must be provided):
        {
            "chat_id":  "<chat doc_id to cancel>",
            "token_id": "<cancellation token UUID>"

    Returns:
        { "cancelled": true,  "method": "chat_id"|"token_id" }

    if not data:

        return {"cancelled": False, "error": "missing chat_id or token_id"}

    chat_id = data.get("chat_id")
    token_id = data.get("token_id")

    if not chat_id and not token_id:

        return {"cancelled": False, "error": "missing chat_id or token_id"}

    if chat_id:
        logger.info("chat_cancel: attempting cancel by chat_id='%s'", chat_id)
        cancelled = CANCELLATION_REGISTRY.cancel(chat_id)
        if cancelled:
            logger.info("chat_cancel: cancelled by chat_id='%s'", chat_id)
            return {"cancelled": True, "method": "chat_id"}

    if token_id:
        logger.info("chat_cancel: attempting cancel by token_id='%s'", token_id)

        if cancelled:

        provider: Optional[str] = None,
        model: Optional[str] = None,

            total_cost_cxjcoins=input_cost + output_cost,

def discover_routers() -> List[dict]:
    """
    Dynamically discover all routers in the api package.
    Each router module should export a 'router' attribute.
    
    Returns:
        List of dicts with 'router', 'prefix', and 'module' keys.
    """
    routers = []
    api_package_path = Path(__file__).parent
    
    # Get all Python files in the api directory (excluding __init__.py and test files)
    router_files = [
        f.stem for f in api_package_path.glob('*.py')
        if f.is_file() and f.stem not in ['__init__', '__pycache__']
        and not f.name.startswith('test_')
    ]
    
    for module_name in sorted(router_files):
        try:
            # Import the module dynamically
            module = importlib.import_module(f'codx.junior.api.{module_name}')
            
            # Check if module has a 'router' attribute
            if hasattr(module, 'router'):
                router_obj = getattr(module, 'router')
                routers.append({
                    'router': router_obj,
                    'prefix': '/api',
                    'module': module_name
                })
                logger.info(f"Loaded router from module: {module_name}")
            else:
                logger.debug(f"Module {module_name} does not export 'router' attribute")
        except ImportError as e:
            logger.error(f"Failed to import router module {module_name}: {e}")
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Error loading router from {module_name}: {e}")
    
    logger.info(f"Successfully discovered {len(routers)} routers")

| Your note | What the document now says |
|---|---|

A **task** is a :class:`~codx.junior.db.Chat` stored in

Creation rules

def discover_routers() -> List[dict]:
    """
    Dynamically discover all routers in the api package.
    Each router module should export a 'router' attribute.
    
    Returns:
        List of dicts with 'router', 'prefix', and 'module' keys.
    """
    routers = []
    api_package_path = Path(__file__).parent
    
    # Get all Python files in the api directory (excluding __init__.py and test files)
    router_files = [
        f.stem for f in api_package_path.glob('*.py')
        if f.is_file() and f.stem not in ['__init__', '__pycache__']
        and not f.name.startswith('test_')
    ]
    
    for module_name in sorted(router_files):
        try:
            # Import the module dynamically
            module = importlib.import_module(f'codx.junior.api.{module_name}')
            
            # Check if module has a 'router' attribute
            if hasattr(module, 'router'):
                router_obj = getattr(module, 'router')
                routers.append({
                    'router': router_obj,
                    'prefix': '/api',
                    'module': module_name
                })
                logger.info(f"Loaded router from module: {module_name}")
            else:
                logger.debug(f"Module {module_name} does not export 'router' attribute")
        except ImportError as e:
            logger.error(f"Failed to import router module {module_name}: {e}")
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Error loading router from {module_name}: {e}")
    
    logger.info(f"Successfully discovered {len(routers)} routers")

"""
Prompt and message construction for chat interactions.

Extracted from ``ChatEngine`` to keep prompt-building logic (history
rendering, refine/agent prompts, current-request wrapping, and response file
extraction) in one place and reduce the size of the engine module.

The key idea is to demote prior conversation turns to inert *context* so the
model does not re-execute instructions that were already processed:

* Prior turns are wrapped in a ``<conversation_history>`` block and their
  assistant messages are labelled ``<assistant_done>``.
* The live instruction is isolated in a ``<current_request>`` block.

Multimodal content
------------------
Messages with attachments are converted into LangChain messages whose
``content`` is a LIST of parts (``{"type": "text"}`` plus one
``{"type": "image_url"}`` per image). Prompt assembly must therefore only
ever rewrite the TEXT part: stringifying the list would replace the images
with their Python representation and make them invisible to the model.
See :meth:`ChatPromptBuilder._get_text_content` /
:meth:`ChatPromptBuilder._set_text_content`.

Conversation attachments
------------------------
``Message.attachments`` must ALWAYS be visible to the model — not only on the
message that happens to be the current request. Because the history block is
rendered as plain text, images carried by prior turns would otherwise be lost.

:meth:`ChatPromptBuilder.collect_attachments` gathers the attachments of EVERY
visible message (parent chats first, then the current chat) and
:meth:`ChatPromptBuilder.build_ai_prompt_messages` appends them to the single
``<current_request>`` message:

* ``image/*`` attachments become ``{"type": "image_url"}`` parts,
* every other type (audio notes, documents) is listed in a ``## Attachments``
  text block ONLY, so the model still knows it exists without the request
  carrying an invalid ``image_url`` part.

Attachment payload normalization
--------------------------------
An ``image_url`` part is only useful when the provider can DECODE it. When it
cannot, models do not fail the request: they replace the image with an
``[Unsupported Image]`` placeholder, which looks like "the AI cannot see my
screenshots". :meth:`ChatPromptBuilder._prepare_attachment` therefore
normalizes every payload before it is sent:

* a ``base64_data`` value that already holds a full ``data:`` URI is not
  prefixed a second time (``data:image/png;base64,data:image/png;base64,...``
  is not decodable),
* whitespace/newlines inside the base64 payload are stripped,
* the media type is resolved from ``file_type`` → data-URI header → file
  extension, so ``application/octet-stream`` / ``image/*`` are never sent,
* only formats vision APIs accept (PNG/JPEG/WEBP/GIF) travel as parts —
  SVG/BMP/TIFF/HEIC are listed in the text block instead,
* oversized screenshots are downscaled/re-encoded (Pillow, best effort,
  cached per payload).

The resulting status of every attachment (mime, size, sent / not sent and
why) is written into the ``## Attachments`` text block.

def debit(
        self,
        cost: float,
        usage: Optional[TokenUsage] = None,
        description: str = "",
    ) -> WalletTransaction:
        """Debit cost from wallet balance, update spending limits, and record transaction."""
        for limit in self.spending_limits:
            limit.consume(cost)
        self.balance_cxjcoins -= cost
        self.updated_at = datetime.utcnow().isoformat()
        tx = WalletTransaction(
            amount_cxjcoins=-cost,
            description=description or "AI model usage charge",
            usage=usage,
            balance_after=self.balance_cxjcoins,
        )
        self.transactions.append(tx)
        return tx

    def credit(self, amount: float, description: str = "") -> WalletTransaction:
        """Add cxjcoins to the wallet balance and record the transaction."""
        self.balance_cxjcoins += amount
        self.updated_at = datetime.utcnow().isoformat()
        tx = WalletTransaction(
            amount_cxjcoins=amount,
            description=description or "Credit",
            balance_after=self.balance_cxjcoins,
        )
        self.transactions.append(tx)
        return tx

    def get_limit_summary(self) -> List[dict]:
        return [
            {
                "period": lim.period.value,
                "limit_cxjcoins": lim.limit_cxjcoins,
                "current_spent": lim.current_spent,
                "remaining": lim.remaining,
            }
            for lim in self.spending_limits
        ]

"""
Chat + AI
This module is responsible for chat persistence and management.

Besides the classic full-chat ``save_chat``, this module now exposes granular,
merge-safe message operations (``add_message``, ``update_message``,
``remove_message``) used to persist chat changes *during* an AI turn (e.g.
tool-usage notification messages, streamed partial responses) without
overwriting concurrent updates.

It also provides full-text search capabilities via the ``search_chats`` method,
delegating to the ``ChatSearcher`` class for filtering by time frame, keyword
matching, and pagination.

Merge strategy (per message, keyed by ``doc_id``):

    ```mermaid
    flowchart TD
        A[Incoming chat messages] --> C{doc_id exists in stored chat?}
        B[Stored chat messages] --> C
        C -->|No| D[Keep message]
        C -->|Yes| E{parse incoming.updated_at >= parse stored.updated_at?}
        E -->|Yes| F[Keep incoming]
        E -->|No| G[Keep stored]
        D --> H[Merged message list]
        F --> H
        G --> H
    ```

CHANGED — timestamp normalisation:
    ``updated_at`` values historically exist in TWO formats:
    ``str(datetime.now())`` (space separator, Message default) and
    ``datetime.isoformat()`` (T separator, stamped by add/update_message).
    Comparing them as raw strings is WRONG ("...T..." always beats "... ..."
    lexicographically for the same day). :func:`_parse_timestamp` parses both
    formats so the last-writer-wins decision uses real datetimes.

CHANGED — persist hot-path:
    The granular operations are now called frequently mid-run (tool events,
    throttled stream persists). :meth:`ChatManager._load_stored_chat` reads
    the chat directly from ``chat.file_path`` when possible instead of
    scanning the whole tasks tree via ``find_by_id``.

    The :meth:`ChatManager.search_chats` method provides full-text search
    across all chat data with optional time-frame filtering, user filtering,
    and pagination, delegating to :class:`codx.junior.chat_searcher.ChatSearcher`.

NEW — chat filtering:
    The :meth:`ChatManager.get_recent_chats` method now supports filtering by
    user_id, board, column, and chat_type (task or chat).

CHANGED — project_ids filtering:

CHANGED — chat ID validation:
    The :meth:`ChatManager.load_chat_from_path` method now ensures all loaded
    chats have a valid ID. Missing IDs are extracted from the filename or

CHANGED — time-range filtering:

# Long running tasks (LRT) — design > Status: **review v2** (incorporates the review notes of 2026-xx) > Owner: ProjectManager · Implementation: `software_developer` / `py_senior` > Prerequisite: milestone **LRT‑0** (preparation, see §10). LRT does not start before LRT‑0 is done. #TL; DR; A **long running task** is one **main task** (a normal kanban task) that carries an objective, a **budget** and a **managing profile**. The system splits the objective into small tasks, processes them one by one, lets the manager create more tasks while it runs, and stops only when **all tasks are done**, the **budget is spent** or a **user stops/pauses it**. Runs survive an app restart and resume alone — no "resume" click. What changed in this review (the notes we received): 1. **The run is anchored on a main task**, not on a free‑text objective. The main task owns the objective, the budget, the managing profile and the pause/stop switch. 2. **All tasks of a run share the same ancestor** (the main task) at any depth — enforced, not assumed. 3. **Pause/Stop lives on the main task** and every descendant turn checks it before running (mid‑turn stop cancels the in‑flight turn). We reviewed encoding it in `Chat.mode` and **rejected it** (see §6). 4. **The blocking defects are fixed first**, in a preparation milestone (LRT‑0), before any LRT code lands. 5. **The kanban storage changes** (single `kanban.json` is too weak): one file per board, immutable ids, atomic writes with a lock, versioned migration. 6. **`AGENT_DONE_WORD` is removed** together with the agent‑iteration logic that depends on it. 7. **The worker runs in the background process only** (the one started with `CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND`). The API process never runs the loop; a file lock guarantees a single worker anyway. Decisions still needed from the user: budget unit (recommend cxjcoins), one task at a time per run (recommend yes), and whether the kanban storage v2 lands before LRT (recommend yes, it is inside LRT‑0). --- ## 1. Scope **In scope (this feature)** - Create a run from an existing or new **main task**: objective, budget, managing profile, board. - Supervisor split → task creation → sequential processing → self‑expansion → completion, all on one board. - Durable run state that survives restarts, power‑offs and the two‑process deployment. - Pause / resume / stop from the main task; hard budget enforcement; stall and loop guards. - API + tool + events so the UI and the managing profile can see and drive the run. **Out of scope (explicitly)** - Parallel task execution inside one run (single worker per run in v1; the tick shape allows it later). - New orchestration infrastructure (Celery/APScheduler/queues). The existing daemon‑thread pattern is enough. - AI sub‑task generation at creation time (`generate_tasks` stays removed: tasks are created with all their information). - Multi‑project runs (a run lives in one project). - A dedicated LRT UI page. v1 reuses the board + a run header on the main task. --- ## 2. Model: the main task *is* the run ``` Run = Chat(main task) + its descendant tree + the board it lives on ``` | Concept | Where it lives | Notes | |---|---|---| | Objective | `Chat.description` + first message of the main task | Human readable, AI readable | | Budget | `Chat.estimation_cost` on the main task | cxjcoins, existing field — already enforced by the agent | | Managing profile | `Chat.profiles` on the main task (`["project_manager"]` by default) | The profile that splits and declares completion | | Run config | `Chat.run` (new optional dict on `Chat`) | `per_task_budget`, `supervisor_reserve`, `max_tasks`, `max_iterations`, `task_mode`, `board_id`, `column`, `verify_column` | | Run state | `Chat.run_status` + `Chat.run_state` (new optional fields) | `running`/`paused`/`stopped`/`completed`/`budget_exhausted`/`failed`/`stalled`, `attempts`, `current_task_id`, `ticks`, `stop_reason` | | Board | `Chat.kanban_id` (id, not name) | One board per run: the board *is* the run's task list | | Ancestor | `Chat.root_id` (new, cached) | `root_id == main task id` for every descendant | Why the main task and not a new entity: **tasks are already chats** (`Chat` has `parent_id`, `profiles`, `cost`, `estimation_cost`, `status_history`, `mode`), and the whole UI (board, planning, chat view, cost) already renders a chat. A second entity would duplicate persistence and break `/api/planning`. ```mermaid flowchart TD M["Main task (Chat)
objective · budget · profile · run_status"] --> T1["Task A"] M --> T2["Task B"] T1 --> T21["Task A.1"] T21 --> T211["Task A.1.1"] M -. root_id = M .-> T1 M -. root_id = M .-> T21 M -. root_id = M .-> T211 ``` --- ## 3. Ancestry: every task shares the main task as ancestor **Invariant:** for every chat that belongs to a run, walking `parent_id` up must reach the main task. Implementation: - **Cached field** `Chat.root_id` (optional). `TaskManager.create_task` sets it: `root_id = parent.root_id or parent.id` when a parent exists, `root_id = self.id` for the main task. - **`codx/junior/identity.py`** exposes the two primitives every caller must use: - `resolve_root_id(chat, chat_manager)` — returns `chat.root_id`, walking `parent_id` when the cache is missing (legacy chats) and backfilling it. - `is_descendant_of(chat, root_id, chat_manager)` — the guard used by the runner and the API. - **Board contents are a strict subset**: a task on the run board whose `root_id` is not the main task is *invalid* and the runner ignores it (logged as a catalogue error, never processed). - Depth is unbounded: A → A.1 → A.1.1 … all resolve to the same main task. --- ## 4. Budget: defined on the main task, enforced everywhere **Unit:** cxjcoins, using the existing `Chat.cost` (monotonic, survives message deletion) and `Chat.estimation_cost` (hard cap already honoured by `SmolAgent`). Two mechanisms, both needed: 1. **Roll‑up (accounting).** `ChatManager._accumulate_message_cost` currently adds a message cost to *its own* chat. It also adds the same delta to the **root chat** (`resolve_root_id`), so the main task's `Chat.cost` is the run total. Consequence: the main task's own `estimation_cost` (= run budget) is already enforced by the agent for every turn the supervisor takes, with no new budget code. 2. **Push‑down (admission).** Before each descendant turn the runner sets the task's `estimation_cost = min(per_task_budget, remaining − reserve)`. A descendant can therefore never overspend the run, and the run can always afford the final report (`supervisor_reserve`). Hard stop rule: if `remaining <= supervisor_reserve` the run finishes as `budget_exhausted` and the supervisor writes the delivery report **without another paid turn** (template + facts, no LLM). `spent` is always **recomputed** from the chats of the run each tick; the persisted counter is informational only (protection against drift and manual edits). --- ## 5. Execution model: one tick at a time ```mermaid flowchart TD T[Tick] --> L{run lock?} L -->|no| X[skip] L -->|yes| S{run_status == running?} S -->|no| X S -->|yes| B{remaining > reserve?} B -->|no| BE[STOP: budget_exhausted + report] B -->|yes| A{actionable task on board?} A -->|yes| R[claim task · estimation_cost = remaining
chat_with_project task] R --> P[persist attempt + heartbeat] P --> T2[next tick] A -->|no| SUP[supervisor turn on the MAIN task
create / move / verify tasks or finish] SUP --> D{finished or stagnant?} D -->|finished| CP[STOP: completed + delivery report] D -->|stagnant| ST[STOP: stalled] D -->|no| T2 ``` - **Actionable task** = `root_id == main.id`, `status in (todo, doing)`, `attempts < MAX_ATTEMPTS (3)`, ordered by priority → due date → `sort_index`. **One at a time**, deliberately: predictable budget, no board/worktree contention. - **Recovery**: if `current_task_id` is set, the process died and no cancellation token exists for it → `attempts += 1` and re‑run. After 3 attempts → `status="onhold"` + `request_help` comment. - **Resumability**: state is on disk (the main task file), the only in‑flight unit is a single chat turn that is itself persisted incrementally (`ChatEventBridge`), and the tick re‑reads everything from disk. A restart resumes the same tick — nothing to re‑create. - **Single worker**: `.codx/tasks//long_running/.lock` created with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL` + `{pid, host, heartbeat}`; a stale lock (heartbeat older than `LOCK_TIMEOUT`) is taken over. Required because **two processes** are alive. ### Where the worker runs The deployment runs **two independent processes**: the API without the flag, and the background service with `CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND` set. Therefore: - the loop (`check_long_running_runs`) is started from `background.start_background_services`, next to `check_projects`, and only when the flag is on; - each run advances inside its own thread with `asyncio.run(runner.tick())`, mirroring `run_project_check_thread`; - the API process only **writes intent** (start/pause/resume/stop) and **reads state** — it never executes a turn, so the 30 s request timeout (`GLOBAL_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`) is irrelevant; - if no worker is running, the status endpoint must answer `"waiting for worker"` instead of pretending the run is progressing. --- ## 6. Control surface: pause / stop on the main task **We reviewed encoding the run state in `Chat.mode` and rejected it.** `mode` is a *prompt selector*: `ChatEngine._resolve_chat_mode_flags` branches on it (`task`/`tutorial` → refine prompt, `agent` → agent prompt, `vibe` → pre‑search). Overloading it with `paused`/`stopped` would make the engine process **descendant tasks with the wrong prompt** and would collide with the mode the task actually needs. | Action | Effect | Persisted where | |---|---|---| | Start | create main task (`mode="long_running"`), board, run fields, `status="todo"` → `run_status="running"` | main task | | Pause | `run_status="paused"`, mirror `Chat.status="onhold"` | main task | | Resume | `run_status="running"`, mirror `Chat.status="doing"` | main task | | Stop | `run_status="stopped"`, mirror `Chat.status="rejected"`, cancel the in‑flight token | main task | | Complete | `run_status="completed"`, `Chat.status="done"`, delivery report message | main task | `mode="long_running"` is safe today: any mode other than `task`/`tutorial`/`agent`/`vibe` falls into the standard chat branch, so the supervisor turn is a normal chat turn with the managing profile composed into the system prompt. **Descendant processing must be reviewed against the switch** — this is the note we received: 1. every tick reads the main task **from disk** before starting a turn (no cached state); 2. `runner._assert_root_running(task)` re‑checks immediately before `chat_with_project`; 3. pause/stop calls `CANCELLATION_REGISTRY.cancel()` so a turn in progress aborts at the next yield point (`CancelledError` is already handled and persisted); 4. a descendant turn started **manually** (a human opens the task and asks something) is allowed but still counted against the budget, and the tick never touches that task while a token exists for it (`is_task_processing`). `run_status` is the single source of truth; `Chat.status` is only the mirror the board and planning views already understand. --- ## 7. Completion and guards - **Only the managing profile finishes a run**, by calling the tool `long_running(action="finish", summary=...)` on its own main task. Validated server‑side (chat is the run's main task **and** the caller's profile is in `main.profiles`). - `finish` appends a **delivery report** message to the main task: what was built, how to test it, files touched, remaining gaps. This is the artefact a human reviews. - Safety nets: `max_tasks`, `max_iterations`, **stagnation** (`STAGNATION_TICKS = 3` supervisor turns that neither create nor move a task → `stalled`), unrecoverable error → `failed`. - The last task of every run should be a **"how to test"** task; the supervisor prompt requires it. --- ## 8. Kanban storage v2 (prerequisite) Today: **one** `.codx/tasks/kanban.json` for every board, written read‑modify‑write with no lock (`ChatManager.save_kanban`), while the UI writes the same file; board **name is also the storage folder** (`get_chat_file`), so a rename `shutil.move`s a folder and rewrites every task. For LRT (which writes board config and run state continuously while the UI edits the same catalogue) this is not acceptable. **v2 layout** ``` .codx/tasks/ index.json { version: 2, boards: [ {id,title,type,parent_id,folder,order} ], tags } boards//board.json { id,title,description,type,parent_id,folder,columns:[{id,title,color,order}],run?:{} } //..json (chats unchanged on disk) long_running/.lock (run lock) ``` - **One file per board**: a write touches a single small file → no cross‑board clobbering. - **Atomic writes** (`tmp` + `os.replace`) and a project‑level file lock (`fcntl`) so the API process and the background process can both write. - **Immutable identity**: `board.id`, `column.id`, `folder` never change. `title` is a label. **A rename no longer moves a folder and no longer rewrites tasks** (fixes the `shutil.move` + `_retarget_board_tasks` behaviour of `project_manager_tools`). - **Task references by id**: `Chat.kanban_id`, `Chat.column_id` become the source of truth; `Chat.board`/`Chat.column` stay as display labels for backward compatibility until the UI is migrated. - **Migration** (`codx/junior/migrations/kanban_v1_to_v2.py`): read the legacy `kanban.json` once, split into board files, assign ids/folders, map `Chat.board → kanban_id`, back up `kanban.v1.backup.json`, idempotent, runs on first load. - **API compatibility**: `GET /api/kanban` keeps returning the assembled legacy shape (the current Vue client keeps working); `POST /api/kanban` writes through the new store (diff‑based). A v2 endpoint (`/api/kanban/boards/{id}`) is added for new work. - Catalogue logic moves to **one** module (`codx/junior/kanban/catalogue.py`) used by `project_manager_tools`, the API and LRT — today the lookups live inside a 2 000‑line tool file. --- ## 9. API and tool surface Identity in the URL, `project_id` as query param, bodies describe the resource only (project REST conventions). | Method | Path | Effect | |---|---|---| | `POST` | `/api/long-running` | `{main_task_id}` (attach to an existing task) **or** `{name, description, budget_cxjcoins, profile, board?}` (create the main task + board) → `run_status="running"` | | `GET` | `/api/long-running` | list runs (main task, run_status, spent/remaining, task counts) | | `GET` | `/api/long-running/{main_task_id}` | detail: state, budget, current task, per‑task table, worker presence | | `POST` | `/api/long-running/{main_task_id}/pause` \| `/resume` \| `/stop` | durable flag (+ cancel in‑flight token on stop) | | `POST` | `/api/long-running/{main_task_id}/tick` | one manual tick (debug/testing; admin only) | | socket | `codx-junior-long-running` | `tick`, `task_started`, `task_done`, `finished`, `budget_exhausted` | Tool `long_running` (registered in `codx/junior/tools/__init__.py`, `session` + `project_settings` injected): - `start` — turn the current chat into a run (objective + budget + profile); - `status` — budget, task table, current step (for the managing profile); - `finish` — **only** the run's own profile on its own main task may complete a run; - `add_task` — thin alias over `project_manager(action="create_task")` with `parent_id = current task`, so the supervisor has one obvious verb and the ancestor invariant is kept automatically. request.description:
## Objective

Make the codebase safe to build **long-running tasks (LRT)** on. Design and decisions: `docs/long-running-tasks.md` (§10 is this task). Nothing of LRT itself is written here — only the fixes and the storage/identity foundations LRT depends on.

Delivery rule (agile): every item below is independently verifiable and the whole batch must leave the app **deployable and demoable** with **no behaviour change for the user**. Ship in the order listed; 0.5/0.6 can run in parallel with 0.2.

## Checklist (blocking, in order)

**0.1 — Broken kanban package import**
`codx/junior/kanban/__init__.py` imports `codx.junior.kanban.board_status_review`, which does not exist in the repo (`kanban/` holds only `__init__.py`), so `import codx.junior.kanban` raises.
→ Implement the module or remove the package/exports. Acceptance: `python -c "import codx.junior.kanban"` succeeds.

**0.2 — Kanban storage v2 + migration + lock**
Today one `.codx/tasks/kanban.json` holds every board, written read-modify-write with no lock (`ChatManager.save_kanban`) while the UI writes the same file; the board *name* is also the storage folder (`get_chat_file`), so a rename `shutil.move`s a folder and rewrites every task (`project_manager_tools._move_board_folder` / `_retarget_board_tasks`).
→ New layout: `.codx/tasks/index.json` + `.codx/tasks/boards/<board_id>/board.json`; atomic writes (`tmp` + `os.replace`); project-level `fcntl` lock; immutable `id`/`folder`, `title` is only a label (rename never moves a folder nor rewrites tasks); catalogue logic in one module `codx/junior/kanban/catalogue.py` used by `project_manager_tools`, the API and LRT.
→ Migration `codx/junior/migrations/kanban_v1_to_v2.py`: split the legacy file, assign ids/folders, map `Chat.board → Chat.kanban_id` (keep `board`/`column` as labels), write `kanban.v1.backup.json`, idempotent, runs on first load.
→ Compatibility: `GET /api/kanban` keeps returning the assembled legacy shape (current Vue client untouched); `POST /api/kanban` writes through the new store.
Acceptance: boards load from the per-board files; two concurrent writers do not lose a board; renaming a board with tasks keeps the tasks visible.

**0.3 — Ancestry: all tasks share the main task**
→ Add `Chat.root_id`; `TaskManager.create_task` sets `root_id = parent.root_id or parent.id` (and `self.id` for a root); add `codx/junior/identity.py` with `resolve_root_id(chat, chat_manager)` (walks `parent_id` when the cache is missing and backfills) and `is_descendant_of(...)`; backfill migration for existing chats.
Acceptance: a 3-level chain (A → A.1 → A.1.1) resolves to the same root; every existing chat resolves a root.

**0.4 — Cost roll-up to the root**
`ChatManager._accumulate_message_cost` adds a message cost to its own chat only. Also add the same delta to the root chat (`resolve_root_id`) so the main task's `Chat.cost` is the run total and `Chat.estimation_cost` on the main task enforces the run budget with the existing agent check.
Acceptance: spending in a child raises the root `Chat.cost` exactly once; deleting a message never reduces it.

**0.5 — Remove `AGENT_DONE_WORD` and the agent-iteration logic (deprecated by decision)**
Remove `globals.AGENT_DONE_WORD`; `chat_prompt_builder.append_agent_message` + the `is_agent` branch of `build_ai_prompt_messages`; step 24 recursion (`is_agent_done`) in `chat_engine._chat_with_project_inner`; the `is_agent` flag in `_resolve_chat_mode_flags`; the `agent` tag in `_build_ai_headers`; `CHAT_MODE_AGENT`; and the `get_agent_max_iterations`/`iterations_left` usage if it becomes dead.
Acceptance: no `AGENT_DONE_WORD` reference remains (`grep -r` empty); a chat with `mode="agent"` behaves as a normal chat and can no longer self-loop.

**0.6 — Delete the dead duplicate sub-task generation**
`engine/chat_engine_actions.generate_tasks`, `CODXJuniorSession.generate_tasks`, the socket handler `codx-junior-subtasks` (it calls a session method that no longer exists) and the legacy `codx/junior/engine.py` module (shadowed by the `codx/junior/engine/` package). Keep `POST /api/chats/sub-tasks` answering 410.
Acceptance: no `generate_tasks` symbol remains; no sio handler calls a missing method.

**0.7 — `CODXJuniorSession.chat_event` is missing**
`api/chat.py` and `sio.py` call `codx_junior_session.chat_event(...)`, but `CODXJuniorSession` no longer defines it, so `POST /api/chats` returns an error object instead of the processed chat.
→ Add the method (delegating to `event_manager.chat_event`) or switch every caller to `event_manager.chat_event`. Acceptance: `POST /api/chats` returns the processed chat.

**0.8 — `ChatManager.find_by_id` substring matching**
It matches `chat_id in path`, so an id that is a prefix of another one loads the wrong chat. Ancestor resolution and the runner must never load the wrong task.
→ Match the exact `.<id>.json` suffix. Acceptance: two chats whose ids share a prefix resolve correctly.

**0.9 — Duplicated handlers**
Two `@app.on_event("startup")` in `app.py` (one starts background services, the other only logs) and `PUT /chats/mark-seen/{chat_id}/{message_id}` defined twice in `api/chat.py`.
→ Keep one of each. Acceptance: one startup handler, one mark-seen route.

**0.10 — Smoke tests**
Import every router through `discover_routers`, catalogue round-trip (create/rename/delete board + column), ancestry resolution, cost roll-up. Acceptance: `pytest` green.

## Out of scope (do not fix here, create separate tasks if you hit them)
`_user_involved_in_chat` reads non-existent `Chat.created_by` / `Message.created_by`; `chat_engine.py` imports `from engine.agent_runtime` (root-level `engine/` package) instead of `codx.junior.engine`; `codx/junior/engine.py` vs `codx/junior/engine/` coexistence beyond the deletion in 0.6.

## Demo (definition of done)
Open the board list loaded from the new store · rename a board that has tasks (no folder move, tasks still visible) · `POST /api/chats` returns a processed chat · `grep -r AGENT_DONE_WORD codx/` empty · `pytest` green. Then LRT-1 can start.

I'll start by checking what LRT-0 actually changed on disk, so the implementation tasks are built on the real code and not on the design assumptions.#TL; DR;

**Status: at risk — not on the code, on the tooling.** Two things came out of this turn that you need to know before we spend money on the implementation:

1. **LRT‑0 is only *mostly* landed.** Storage v2, `root_id`, cost roll‑up and the `find_by_id` fix are in the repo. But `AGENT_DONE_WORD` is still in `globals.py` and still drives the recursion in `chat/chat_engine.py`, `generate_tasks` is still alive in `chat_engine_actions.py` / sio / `app.py`, and the duplicated `on_event("startup")` + mark‑seen routes are still there. I have written all of that into a cleanup work package (WP0) instead of assuming it was done.
2. **I could not start the work automatically.** The cards I created were persisted under the **owner project of this chat** (`d4e4b4a9` — the root `codx-junior` project), so the `codx-api` board cannot see them, `update_task` says "not found" and `process_task` refuses them. The work packages exist; they are just parked on the wrong project's board. **One decision from you unblocks everything** (see §Decisions) — my recommendation is option **2**.

The plan itself is written down and cannot get lost: `docs/long-running-tasks-plan.md`.

---

## 1. What actually exists now

    """
    Compute (and stamp) the ``root_id`` of *chat* from its parent.

    Creation rules:

    * a chat without a parent is its own root (``root_id = chat.id``),
    * a child inherits ``parent.root_id`` when the parent already knows its

    * nothing is inherited from a parent that is not there.

        >>> attach_root_id(child, parent)          # parent is the main task

        >>> attach_root_id(main_task, None)        # no parent: it is the root

    if chat is None:

    if root_id and chat.root_id != root_id:

request.name: LRT-0 residue — remove AGENT_DONE_WORD agent loop and dead sub-task generation
request.description:
## Context
Milestone LRT-0 (preparation for long-running tasks) is reported as done, but the repository still contains the residue that LRT-1 depends on being gone. Verified on disk:
- `codx/junior/globals.py` still defines `AGENT_DONE_WORD = "$$@@AGENT_DONE@@$$$"`.
- `codx/junior/chat/chat_engine.py` still contains the `is_agent_done = AGENT_DONE_WORD in response_message.content` branch and the recursive `chat_with_project(... iteration + 1)` call, plus the `if is_agent: tags.append("agent")` header and the agent refine message that asks the model to "Return { AGENT_DONE_WORD }".
- `codx/junior/engine/chat_engine_actions.py` still implements `generate_tasks` (with `SubTaskStatus` / `TaskGenerationStatus`), `codx/junior/sio/sio.py` still registers `codx-junior-subtasks`, and `app.py` still has `@app.post("/api/chats/sub-tasks")` calling `codx_junior_session.generate_tasks`.
- `codx/junior/app.py` still has duplicated/legacy handlers (two `@app.on_event("startup")`, legacy `/api/chats`, `/api/kanban` duplicates of `codx/junior/api/chat.py`), and `api/chat.py` defines mark-seen twice.

## Objective
Remove the deprecated agent-iteration machinery and the dead sub-task generation so the engine has exactly one way to drive a chat, then de-duplicate the startup hook and the routes.

## Steps
1. **Agent logic.** Delete `AGENT_DONE_WORD` from `codx/junior/globals.py` and every reference: `chat_engine.py` (`is_agent_done`, `if is_agent and not is_agent_done and iterations_left` recursion, the `"agent"` tag in `_build_ai_headers`, the `is_agent` refine prompt block), `chat_prompt_builder.append_agent_message`, `build_ai_prompt_messages(is_agent=...)` parameter, `_resolve_chat_mode_flags` `is_agent`, and the `CHAT_MODE_AGENT` constant / `get_agent_max_iterations` usage. A chat with `mode="agent"` must behave like a normal chat and can no longer loop on itself.
2. **Dead sub-task generation.** Remove `ChatEngineActions.generate_tasks` and the `SubTaskStatus` / `TaskGenerationStatus` helpers if nothing else uses them, `CODXJuniorSession.generate_tasks`, the sio handler `codx-junior-subtasks`, and the `/api/chats/sub-tasks` handlers. The endpoint may stay as a `410 Gone` stub (one place only) but must never call a missing method.
3. **De-duplicate.** One `@app.on_event("startup")` in `app.py` (keep the one that actually starts what the product needs: socket/session init and `start_background_services`), one `PUT /chats/mark-seen/{chat_id}/{message_id}` in `api/chat.py`, and no `/api/chats`/`/api/kanban` handler duplicated in both `app.py` and `api/chat.py` (the API module is auto-discovered — keep that one).

## Acceptance criteria
- `grep -rn "AGENT_DONE_WORD" codx/` returns nothing.
- `grep -rn "generate_tasks" codx/` returns only comments/docstrings (no call sites, no sio handler).
- `python -c "import codx.junior.chat.chat_engine, codx.junior.engine.session, codx.junior.api.chat, codx.junior.sio.sio"` succeeds.
- Only one `on_event("startup")` and one mark-seen route remain (`grep -c` proof in the PR description).
- No behaviour change for a normal chat: a `mode="agent"` chat answers once, like `mode="chat"`.

## Out of scope
The long-running feature itself (LRT-1), kanban storage (already v2), `root_id`, cost roll-up.

## Files
codx/junior/globals.py · codx/junior/chat/chat_engine.py · codx/junior/chat/chat_prompt_builder.py · codx/junior/engine/chat_engine_actions.py · codx/junior/engine/session.py · codx/junior/engine.py · codx/junior/sio/sio.py · codx/junior/api/chat.py · codx/junior/app.py · docs/long-running-tasks.md (tick item 0.5/0.6 as done)

request.name: LRT-1.1 — Run model, run store (lock) and run service (start/pause/resume/stop/status)
request.description:
## Context
Design: `docs/long-running-tasks.md` (§2 model, §4 budget, §5 execution, §6 control). Read it first — it is the contract.
A run is a **main task** (`Chat`) that owns the objective (`description`), the budget (`Chat.estimation_cost`), the managing profile (`Chat.profiles`) and the pause/stop switch. All tasks of the run are chats whose `Chat.root_id` is the main task id (`codx/junior/identity.py` already provides `resolve_root_id` / `is_descendant_of`, and `ChatManager` already rolls descendant cost up into the root chat).

## Objective
Add the persistence and the control service of a run — no execution yet. Everything must be importable and unit-testable without AI calls.

## Steps
1. **`codx/junior/db.py`** — extend `Chat` with the run fields, documented in the project style (Field description, why it exists):
   - `run: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None` — run configuration: `per_task_budget`, `supervisor_reserve`, `max_tasks`, `max_iterations`, `task_mode`, `board_id`, `column`, `created_at`, `created_by`.
   - `run_status: str = ''` — `''` when the chat is not a run, else one of the statuses below.
   - `run_state: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None` — durable runtime state: `attempts` (task_id → int), `current_task_id`, `step_started_at`, `last_tick_at`, `ticks`, `stagnant_ticks`, `stop_reason`, `finished`, `delivery_report_message_id`.
2. **`codx/junior/long_running/__init__.py` + `models.py`** — pydantic models + docstrings + a mermaid diagram: `LongRunStatus` (`running`, `paused`, `stopped`, `completed`, `budget_exhausted`, `failed`, `stalled`), `TERMINAL_STATUSES`, `LongRunConfig`, `LongRunState`, `LongRunProgress` (`spent`, `remaining`, `budget`, `tasks_total`, `tasks_done`, `tasks_open`, `current_task_id`, `worker_present`), request models (`StartRunRequest`, `RunControlRequest`). `ConfigDict(str_strip_whitespace=True)` and bounds on numeric fields.
3. **`codx/junior/long_running/store.py`** — atomic, cross-process safe run plumbing:
   - `RunLock(tasks_path, main_task_id)`: lock file `.codx/tasks/long_running/<main_task_id>.lock`, created with `os.open(..., O_CREAT|O_EXCL)`, content `{pid, host, started_at, heartbeat_at}`, `touch()` heartbeat, `release()`, and **stale takeover** when the heartbeat is older than `LOCK_TIMEOUT` (600s) or the pid no longer exists. Context manager `with RunLock(...) as acquired:` returning a bool — never raise when the lock is busy.
   - `load_run_chat(chat_manager, main_task_id)` — reload from disk (never trust a cached chat; the API process writes intent, the worker reads it) and `save_run_chat(chat_manager, chat)` — persist through `ChatManager.save_chat`.
   - Make sure the `long_running` folder can never be read as a board or a chat (`ChatManager.chat_paths` / `KanbanStore.board_dirs` must ignore it — patch if needed).
4. **`codx/junior/long_running/service.py`** — `LongRunningService(settings, session=None)`:
   - `start(...)`: accept `main_task_id` **or** create the main task (`TaskManager.create_task`, `mode="long_running"`, `profiles=[profile]`, `board=<new board>`, `column=...`, `description=<objective>`), set `estimation_cost=budget`, `run=<config>`, `run_status="running"`, `status="todo"`. When a new board is needed, create it through the **existing catalogue helpers** in `codx/junior/tools/project_manager_tools.py` / `ChatManager.load_kanban` + `save_kanban` (read them first, reuse `validate_task_destination`) — never hand-edit `kanban.json`.
   - `pause` / `resume` / `stop`: write the durable flag on the main task **and mirror `Chat.status`** (`onhold` / `doing` / `rejected`); `stop` also cancels the in-flight token via `CANCELLATION_REGISTRY.cancel(<current_task_id>)`.
   - `status(main_task_id)` / `list_runs()`: aggregate from chats — `spent = sum(chat.cost for chat in chats where identity.resolve_root_id(chat) == main_task_id)` (include the main task itself), `remaining = budget - spent`, task counts by `codx.junior.planning_manager.DONE_STATUSES` / `CLOSED_STATUSES` / `STATUS_ORDER` (**never a second hardcoded status list**), `current_task_id`, and `worker_present` (whether the background process is running — derive from `CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND` / the lock heartbeat, and return `"waiting for worker"` when there is none).
   - Validate: only a chat with a non-empty `run_status` is a run; a `main_task_id` that is a descendant (root_id != its own id) is rejected with a clear `ValueError`.

## Acceptance criteria
- `python -c "import codx.junior.long_running, codx.junior.long_running.service"` works, no circular import (do not import `codx.junior.engine` at module level).
- Two `RunLock` instances for the same run: the second one does not acquire while the first holds it; after a heartbeat older than `LOCK_TIMEOUT` it does.
- `start` on a fresh objective creates exactly one board, one main task with `root_id == id`, `run_status == "running"` and `estimation_cost == budget`; `pause`/`resume`/`stop` change `run_status` and the mirrored `Chat.status`.
- `status()` returns the same `spent` as the sum of the chats' `cost` (assert in a test with fake chats).
- All public functions have docstrings in the existing style; type hints everywhere.

## Out of scope
Executing tasks (LRT-1.2), the HTTP router and the tool (LRT-1.3), tests suite (LRT-1.4 covers them, but leave the code testable).

## Files
codx/junior/db.py · codx/junior/long_running/{__init__,models,store,service}.py · codx/junior/kanban/store.py (only if the folder exclusion is needed)

request.description:
## Context
Design: `docs/long-running-tasks.md` §5 (execution model), §4 (budget), §6 (control). Depends on LRT-1.1 (`Chat.run` / `run_status` / `run_state`, `codx/junior/long_running/{models,store,service}.py`). **Do not start before LRT-1.1 is merged.**
The deployment runs **two processes**: the API without the flag and the background service with `CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND` set. The loop runs **only** in the background process; the API only writes intent and reads state.

## Objective
Implement the resumable tick that advances a run one unit of work at a time, and wire it into `codx/junior/background.py`.

## Steps
1. **`codx/junior/long_running/runner.py` — `LongRunningRunner(settings, session=None)`**, `async def tick(self, main_task_id) -> dict` (returns a status dict, never raises for a normal stop):
   - Acquire `RunLock`; if busy → `{"skipped": "locked"}`.
   - Reload the main task **from disk** (`store.load_run_chat`); only `run_status == "running"` proceeds.
   - Budget admission: `spent = Σ chats cost of the run`, `remaining = budget - spent`; when `remaining <= supervisor_reserve` → `run_status = "budget_exhausted"` + a **template delivery report message** (no LLM call) and stop.
   - Task selection: chats on the run board whose `identity.resolve_root_id(chat) == main_task_id`, `status` in the actionable states of `codx.junior.planning_manager` (`todo`/`doing`), `attempts[task_id] < MAX_ATTEMPTS (3)`, ordered priority → due_date → sort_index; ignore (and log) a task of the board whose root is not the main task. **One task per tick.**
   - Before the turn: `task.estimation_cost = min(per_task_budget, remaining - supervisor_reserve)`, save the task, persist `run_state.current_task_id` + `step_started_at` + `ticks += 1` on the main task, emit the `task_started` event.
   - Run the turn: `session.chat_with_project(chat=task)` (build the session with `CODXJuniorSession(settings=...)` when none is injected). Handle `CancelledError` and exceptions: `attempts += 1`; after 3 attempts set the task `onhold` with a `project_manager(action="request_help")`-style comment.
   - No actionable task → **supervisor turn on the main task** (the managing profile splits/creates/verifies tasks) and stagnation detection: a supervisor turn that neither creates nor moves a task increments `run_state.stagnant_ticks`; at `STAGNATION_TICKS (3)` → `run_status="stalled"`.
   - Completion: `run_state.finished` is set by the `long_running` tool (LRT-1.3) → `run_status="completed"`. Guard rails: `max_tasks`, `max_iterations`.
   - Persist state + `heartbeat` before releasing the lock; emit `tick`, `task_done`, `finished`, `budget_exhausted` events.
2. **Events.** Use `EventManager.chat_event(chat=main_task, message=..., event_type=...)` for the human line and `SessionChannel.send_event("codx-junior-long-running", {...})` for the UI (copy the pattern used by `codx/junior/sio/sio.py` / `sio_send_event`).
3. **`codx/junior/background.py`.** Add `LONG_RUNNING_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 5`, `check_long_running_runs()` (loop: `find_all_projects()` → for each project find chats with `run_status == "running"` → submit `run_long_running_tick` to the existing `ThreadPoolExecutor` pattern) and `run_long_running_tick(settings, main_task_id)` running `asyncio.run(runner.tick(...))`. Start the thread inside `start_background_services` next to `check_projects`, guarded by `CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND` and stopped by `RUN_BACKGROUND_PROCESSES` / `stop_event`. **Never start it in the API process.**
4. **Resumability.** Prove it: state lives on the main task file; after a restart the next tick reads `current_task_id`, sees no `CANCELLATION_REGISTRY` token for it, increments `attempts` and continues. Nothing may be held in memory between ticks.

## Acceptance criteria
- Two workers (two processes) never run the same task turn: second one skips with `locked`.
- Killing the process in the middle of a task and restarting resumes the run without any manual action and without duplicating tasks.
- A run whose budget is exhausted stops with `run_status="budget_exhausted"` and a report message, and never spends more than `budget` (verify with `Chat.cost` on the main task).
- `pause` / `stop` from LRT-1.1 is honoured **before** a turn starts and cancels an in-flight turn (`CANCELLATION_REGISTRY.cancel`).
- No tick does more than one `chat_with_project` per task turn; every tick writes `last_tick_at`.
- Docstrings in the existing style, `logger` used instead of prints, no bare `except`.

## Out of scope
HTTP router, LLM tool, supervisor prompt (LRT-1.3). Tests suite (LRT-1.4).

## Files
codx/junior/long_running/runner.py · codx/junior/background.py · codx/junior/ai/cancellation.py (read only) · codx/junior/planning_manager.py (read only) · codx/junior/engine/session.py (chat_with_project)

request.name: LRT-1.3 — API router, long_running tool and supervisor profile
request.description:
## Context
Design: `docs/long-running-tasks.md` §9 (API and tool surface), §7 (completion). Depends on LRT-1.1 (service) and benefits from LRT-1.2 (runner) — but the router must return in < 30s (**`GLOBAL_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` middleware**), so it only writes intent and reads state; it never executes a turn.

## Objective
Expose the run to the API, the UI and the managing profile, and give the supervisor its instructions.

## Steps
1. **`codx/junior/api/long_running.py`** — new `router = APIRouter()`; it is auto-discovered by `codx.junior.api.discover_routers` and mounted at `/api`, so paths are declared without the `/api` prefix. Follow the project REST conventions (identity in the URL, `project_id` as **query** param, bodies describe the resource only):
   - `GET /long-running` — list runs with `status` summary (budget, spent, counts, `worker_present`).
   - `POST /long-running` — `{main_task_id}` **or** `{name, description, budget_cxjcoins, profile, board?, column?, per_task_budget_cxjcoins?, supervisor_reserve_cxjcoins?, max_tasks?, max_iterations?, auto_start?}` → creates/starts the run through `LongRunningService`.
   - `GET /long-running/{main_task_id}` — detail: state, budget, current task, per-task table (`name`, `status`, `cost`, `root_ok`).
   - `POST /long-running/{main_task_id}/pause` | `/resume` | `/stop` — durable flag (+ cancel in-flight token on stop).
   - `POST /long-running/{main_task_id}/tick` — one manual tick (admin only; `asyncio.to_thread`/`run_in_executor` so the event loop is not blocked, and it must return quickly with `{"queued": true}`).
   - Map `ValueError` → 400, missing run → 404, unauthorised → 403; request models with `ConfigDict(str_strip_whitespace=True)` and bounds.
2. **`codx/junior/tools/long_running_tools.py`** + registration in `codx/junior/tools/__init__.py` (`ToolSettings(project_settings=True, session=True, dual_response=True, scope="chat")`), same shape as `project_manager_tools.py`:
   - `start` — turn the current chat (or a new one) into a run: objective + budget + profile.
   - `status` — budget remaining, task table, current step.
   - `finish` — **validated server-side**: only a chat whose `id == main_task_id` **and** whose `profiles` intersect `chat.profiles` may complete the run; sets `run_state.finished`, `run_status="completed"`, `status="done"` and appends the **delivery report** message (what was built, how to test it, files touched, remaining gaps).
   - `add_task` — thin alias over `project_manager(action="create_task")` with `parent_id = current task`, so the ancestor invariant (`root_id`) is kept automatically.
3. **`codx/junior/profiles/long_running.profile`** — supervisor instructions (same file format as the other profiles under `codx/junior/profiles/`): the objective, the remaining budget, the task table, and the rules — *split only what is needed now*, *always leave a verifiable next step*, *always end with a "how to test" task*, *call `finish` only when the objective is demonstrably achieved*, *never exceed the remaining budget*.

## Acceptance criteria
- `GET /api/long-running` and the detail endpoint answer in milliseconds with the background process **off** (`worker_present: false`).
- `POST /api/long-running` with an objective creates the main task + board and returns the run; the API process never executes a turn.
- `finish` from any other chat is rejected with a clear error; `finish` from the run's own main task completes it and appends the delivery report.
- The tool appears in `GET /api/profiles/tools` and in `TOOLS`.
- OpenAPI shows the routes once (no duplicate registration with `app.py`).

## Out of scope
The UI (LRT-3), the runner internals (LRT-1.2), tests (LRT-1.4).

## Files
codx/junior/api/long_running.py · codx/junior/api/__init__.py (read) · codx/junior/tools/long_running_tools.py · codx/junior/tools/__init__.py · codx/junior/profiles/long_running.profile · codx/junior/tools/project_manager_tools.py (read)

request.name: LRT-1.4 — Tests and 5-minute demo of the run skeleton
request.description:
## Context
Definition of Done for milestone LRT-1: tests green + deployed to the demo environment + demo script written + acceptance criteria demonstrated. Depends on LRT-1.1, LRT-1.2 and LRT-1.3.

## Objective
Prove the run skeleton works **offline** (no AI calls) with tests, and write the 5-minute demo management will watch.

## Steps
1. **Tests** (follow the existing `tests/` layout and the `py_test` profile conventions; `pytest`, no network, no LLM):
   - `test_run_lock`: second worker cannot acquire; stale heartbeat (older than `LOCK_TIMEOUT`) is taken over; release frees it.
   - `test_run_ancestry`: a 3-level task chain created with `TaskManager.create_task` resolves the same `root_id`; a task on the run board with a foreign root is **not** selected by the runner.
   - `test_run_budget`: `spent` = Σ `Chat.cost`; admission sets `estimation_cost = min(per_task_budget, remaining - reserve)`; exhausted budget stops the run with `budget_exhausted` and writes the report **without** an LLM call.
   - `test_run_service`: `start` / `pause` / `resume` / `stop` transition `run_status` and mirror `Chat.status`; a non-run chat is rejected.
   - `test_runner_recovery`: a fake session (monkeypatched `chat_with_project`) lets the tick run twice — the second tick must not duplicate the turn, `attempts` increments after a simulated crash, and after `MAX_ATTEMPTS` the task goes `onhold`.
   - `test_runner_stagnation`: 3 supervisor turns without changes → `stalled`.
2. **Demo script** `docs/long-running-tasks-demo.md` (max one screen): steps, data to use, acceptance criteria demonstrated, questions for management. Suggested flow:
   1. `POST /api/long-running` with a tiny objective ("add a README badge") and a small budget → the board and the main task appear.
   2. The worker splits 2–3 tasks; the board shows them; the first one runs and completes.
   3. Kill the background process mid-run → restart → the run continues alone (no "resume" click).
   4. `POST /pause` → nothing moves; `POST /resume` → it moves again; `POST /stop` → a task in flight is cancelled.
   5. Lower the budget to force `budget_exhausted` and show the delivery report message.
3. **Report** which acceptance criteria are covered by a test and which are covered only by the demo.

## Acceptance criteria
- `pytest tests/ -k "run_"` green in CI-like conditions (no AI, no network) and fast (< 30s).
- Demo script exists, is one screen long, and every step has an expected visible result.
- No production code changed unless a test exposes a real defect (then fix it with the owning profile's conventions and note it in the description).

## Out of scope
LRT-2 (autonomy: self-expansion, finish flow, stall policy tuning) and LRT-3 (board run header, socket UI).

## Files
tests/ (new tests) · docs/long-running-tasks-demo.md · docs/long-running-tasks.md

request.content:
Long-running tasks (LRT) contract — design in `docs/long-running-tasks.md`.

- A **run is a main task** (`Chat`): objective in `description`, budget in `estimation_cost`, managing profile in `profiles`, switch in `run_status`/`run_state`/`run`.
- Every sub-task is a chat whose `Chat.root_id` is the main task id (`codx/junior/identity.py`); a task on the run board with a foreign root is never processed.
- Cost is monotonic on `Chat.cost` and rolls up to the root chat, so the main task budget covers the whole tree.
- The **worker loop runs only in the background process** (`CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND`) via `codx/junior/long_running/runner.py`; the API process only writes intent/reads state (30s request timeout).
- Single worker per run enforced by `.codx/tasks/long_running/<main_task_id>.lock`.
- Kanban catalogue is v2 (`tasks/index.json` + `tasks/boards/<id>/board.json`); board/column `id` and `folder` are immutable, titles are labels.
- Statuses come from `planning_manager.STATUS_ORDER` — never hardcode a second list.
- Milestones: LRT-0 prep (done), LRT-1 run skeleton, LRT-2 autonomy, LRT-3 visibility.
